chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: O Muhammad! The people will continue to engage in logical reasoning until they begin discussing the Essence of Allah. When you hear them doing so, say: There is no god but Allah, the One, and nothing whatsoever is like unto Him.

key_terms.لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ: Nothing is like unto Him (divine incomparability)

ai.seo_question: How should one respond when people begin debating the Essence of Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* highlights the Shia principle of *ta'wil* (interpretation) versus *ta'til* (negation), warning against *ghuluw* (exaggeration) in describing Allah's essence. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes the *Kalimah* of pure monotheism as the ultimate corrective when theological discourse shifts from attributes to the incomparable essence, reinforcing the boundary between rational inquiry and divine transcendence.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 10. And with the same chain of transmission, on the authority of Ibn Abu `Umayr, on the authority of Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Muslim

that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) said: “O Muhammad! Always use logic with the people until they start discussing the Essence of Allah. When you hear them talking about that say: There is no god but Allah, the One, and nothing whatsoever is like unto Him.”
